title: Mastic
summary: Mastic is a Brookhaven placename associated with the Mastic Peninsula and especially the Forge River, interpreted as a great river or great tidal river.
address_label: General Forge River / Mastic Peninsula area, Brookhaven, NY
introduction_content: Mastic is associated with a broad neck of land in Brookhaven.
history_content: The placename is tied to early land descriptions that name the river called Mastick. The surrounding peninsula is also part of Unkechaug homeland history, so The placename belongs alongside existing Mastic-area Unkechaug places rather than as a replacement for them.
translation_content:
Recorded forms include Mastick, Mastuck, Mastyc, and Mastic. The name is interpreted from roots meaning great and tidal river, giving the sense of a great river or great tidal river.

Wegonthotak or Wegonthotuck is recorded as a Forge River form interpreted as at the bend or winding of the river.

Why Place Names Matter

“Indigenous place names reveal information about the area’s geography, history and sometimes ecology. Names connect the land to the culture, while acknowledging the contributions of Indigenous people.”

— Caroline Barlott, Naming Amiskwaskahegan: Why Edmonton’s place names matter (2017), Article opening summary
whereintheworld_content: Map location note: The pin is placed near the Forge River estuary because the name originally belonged to the waterway or cove east of the neck; it is not an exact boundary for the Mastic Peninsula or Unkechaug homeland.
